territorial_scope.description: Directs U.S. executive agencies and covers AI infrastructure on Federal sites within the United States; Sec. 10 concerns engagement with allies abroad and imposes no obligations on foreign actors.

evidence.quote: sites on Federal land managed by their respective agencies

summary.short: Directs federal agencies to enable AI data centers and supporting power infrastructure on Federal land, using competitive lease solicitations, clean-power, security and labor conditions, accelerated permitting and grid measures, effective from 14 January 2025.
summary.long: This order sets federal policy to enable AI infrastructure, including data centers, under five principles: national security, competitiveness, clean power, consumer electricity costs, and labor and community benefits. Sec. 3 defines AI data center and related terms. Sec. 4 directs the Defense and Energy Secretaries to identify Federal sites and run competitive solicitations for private leases, with winners subject to conditions on new clean power, hourly matching, cybersecurity and lab security, a memorandum of understanding with the AI Safety Institute, investment reporting and limits, and national-security access to models. Sec. 4(i) requires Defense Department regulations on heightened safeguards for computing hardware at sites it manages, with penalties; Interior must identify BLM sites and designate at least five Priority Geothermal Zones. Secs. 5 to 9 direct reports on electricity prices, transmission and interconnection reporting, expedited NEPA, Clean Air Act and Clean Water Act permitting, endangered-species consultation, transformer supply measures, nationwide permit review, nuclear deployment sites, distributed-energy model contracts and a voluntary power-usage target below 1.1. Sec. 10 directs a State Department plan for allied AI infrastructure; Sec. 11 creates no enforceable rights. Deadlines run from 14 January 2025 to 2027.

notes: The document shows no order number; 14141 comes from registry metadata. The registry status 'repealed' is not stated in the text, so no repeal relation or event is recorded here. Internal inconsistency: Executive Order 14110 is dated October 30, 2023 in Sec. 2(b) but November 1, 2023 in Sec. 4(h)(iv). Most operative provisions direct named agencies; the Sec. 4(h) lease and contract terms reach non-Federal parties only through agency lease or contract terms. Sec. 3(a) excludes independent regulatory agencies from the term agency. Sec. 11(b) makes implementation subject to applicable law and appropriations; Sec. 11(c) states that the order creates no enforceable rights. Definitions refer to external instruments (CFR, Public Laws, FERC orders, CHIPS NOFO) that are not all listed as relations. Consultation-only bodies (e.g., Attorney General, Director of National Intelligence, CEQ, Tribal Nations) are not listed as entities.

The term “agency” means each agency described in 44 U.S.C. 3502(1), except for the independent regulatory agencies described in 44 U.S.C. 3502(5).
The term “AI data center” means a data center used primarily with respect to developing or operating AI.

The term “AI infrastructure” refers collectively to AI data centers, generation and storage resources procured to deliver electrical energy to data centers, and transmission facilities developed or upgraded for the same purpose.

The term “AI model” means a component of an information system that implements AI technology and uses computational, statistical, or machine-learning techniques to produce outputs from a given set of inputs.

The term “clean energy” or “clean energy generation resources” means generation resources that produce few or no emissions of carbon dioxide during operation, including when paired with clean storage technologies.
The term “clean power” means electricity generated by the generation resources described in subsection (e) of this section.
The term “clean repowering” means the practice of siting new clean generation sources at a site with an existing point of interconnection and generation sources operating with fossil fuels
The term “critical electric infrastructure information” has the same meaning as set forth in 18 C.F.R.
The term “data center” means a facility used to store, manage, process, and disseminate electronic information for a computer network,
The term “distributed energy resource” has the same meaning as set forth in 18 C.F.R. 35.28(b)(10).
The term “Federal Permitting Agencies” refers to the agency members of the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council (Permitting Council)

definitions.term: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program

evidence.quote: The term “Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program” refers to the program established to provide an approach for the adoption and use of cloud services by the Federal Government

The term “frontier AI data center” means an AI data center capable of being used to develop, within a reasonable time frame, an AI model with characteristics related either to performance or to the computational resources used in its development
The term “frontier AI infrastructure” means AI infrastructure for which the relevant data center is a frontier AI data center.
The term “frontier AI training” refers to the act of developing an AI model with characteristics related either to performance or to the computational resources used in its development
The term “generation resource” means a facility that produces electricity.
The term “lab-security measures” refers to steps to detect, prevent, or mitigate physical, cyber, or other threats to the operation of a data center,

definitions.defined_in: CHIPS Incentives Program Notice of Funding Opportunity, 2023-NIST-CHIPS-CFF-01

evidence.quote: The term “leading-edge logic semiconductors” refers to semiconductors produced at high volumes using extreme ultraviolet lithography tools as defined by the CHIPS Incentives Program Notice of Funding Opportunity, 2023-NIST-CHIPS-CFF-01.
The term “model weight” means a numerical parameter within an AI model that helps determine the model’s outputs in response to inputs.
The term “non-Federal parties” refers to private-sector entities that enter into a contract with the Department of Defense or the Department of Energy pursuant to section 4(g) of this order.

The term “priority geothermal zone” refers to lands with high potential for the development of geothermal power generation resources, as designated by the Secretary of the Interior, including pursuant to section 4(c) of this order.
The term “project labor agreement” means a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement that establishes the terms and conditions of a construction project.

The terms “transmission facilities” and “transmission infrastructure” mean equipment or structures, including transmission lines and related facilities, used for the purpose of delivering electricity.
The term “transmission organization” refers to a Regional Transmission Organization or an Independent System Operator.

The term “transmission provider” means an entity that manages or operates transmission facilities for the delivery of electric energy used primarily by the public and that is not a transmission organization.
The term “waters of the United States” has the same meaning as set forth in 33 C.F.R. 328.3(a).
